title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Greatland Personnel
tiers.description: All full-time, part-time and casual employees, contractors, consultants and advisers of Greatland Resources Limited and Group companies, as well as all Restricted Persons. Bound by the general prohibition (1.2, 2.1) and by the bans on short-term trading, short selling and hedging (2.2), but not by the Trading Window / Dealing Approval regime.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Directors, officers, KMPs, PDMRs and the Company Secretary of Greatland and Group companies, plus other Group employees designated by the Managing Director and Company Secretary, and persons associated with them (close family; entities, trusts or investment vehicles they control, materially influence or benefit from; business and other associates). Prohibited from Dealing at all unless permitted by the remainder of the Policy.

tiers.name: Directors, PDMRs, Company Secretary
tiers.description: Directors, PDMRs (senior officers with regular access to inside information and power to take managerial decisions) and the Company Secretary, and persons associated with them. They have no general declared Trading Window: their Trading Window is only the period in which a Dealing Approval applies, and approval comes from the Chair (or in their absence the Deputy Chair or Managing Director).

tiers.name: Other Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Restricted Persons who are not Directors, PDMRs or the Company Secretary. They may Deal without a specific Dealing Approval during a Trading Window declared by the Chair; outside a Trading Window they need a Dealing Approval from the Managing Director (direct reports) or otherwise the Company Secretary.

tiers.name: PDMRs
tiers.description: Persons discharging managerial responsibilities for MAR/AIM purposes: a Director, or a senior officer who is not a Director but has regular access to inside information and power to take managerial decisions affecting the Company's future development. Subject to the additional MAR Closed Periods, the exceptional-circumstances-only approval gate, and FCA/RNS notification.

tiers.name: persons closely associated (PCA)
tiers.description: A PDMR's spouse or civil partner; a child or step-child under 18 who is unmarried and has no civil partner; a relative sharing the household for at least a year; and a legal person, trust or partnership managed by, controlled by, set up for the benefit of, or whose economic interests are substantially equivalent to those of, such a person. They must not Deal except during a Trading Window and must notify the Company Secretary immediately.

definitions.hedging_definition: entering into an arrangement if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the person's remuneration that has not vested or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

windows.end_anchor: publication of the Company's annual results
publication of the Company's half-yearly results

windows.start_anchor: any time which is not a Trading Window (the default state: Dealing is prohibited unless a Trading Window has been declared or a Dealing Approval is held)
windows.end_anchor: declaration of a Trading Window or grant of a Dealing Approval

windows.start_anchor: commencement of a Prohibited Period (Company holds information disclosable under ASX LR 3.1, MAR art 17(1) or AIM Rule 11 but withheld in reliance on an exemption)
windows.end_anchor: the information ceases to be withheld

windows.start_anchor: typically two Business Days after release of the annual, half yearly or quarterly results, release of a prospectus, the AGM, or other times at the Chair's discretion, as declared in writing by the Chair (or Deputy Chair or Managing Director)
windows.end_anchor: expiry of the stipulated period, or two weeks if none is stipulated, or earlier written closure by the Chair

windows.start_anchor: grant of a Dealing Approval (a Dealing Approval is deemed to have been given during a declared Trading Window)
windows.end_anchor: expiry of the two Business Day Validity Period, or earlier written shortening

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Chair (or in their absence the Deputy Chair or Managing Director) may at any time, by written notification to relevant Restricted Persons, close a declared Trading Window, and may shorten the Validity Period of any Dealing Approval by written notice. Separately, under 2.1 Greatland may give notice to any or all Greatland Personnel that they must not deal, either for a specified period or until further notice. Prohibited Periods arise automatically and confidentially whenever the Company is withholding disclosable information under ASX LR 3.1A, MAR art 17(4) or the AIM Rule 11 guidance notes.

rules.detail: There is no express derivatives rule. 'Securities' expressly includes derivative instruments, other linked financial instruments and 'instruments to limit the economic risk of other securities held', with no venue limitation, so an OTC put or call over Greatland shares is a Security; entering into, amending or terminating any agreement (even conditional) in respect of Securities is a Dealing. Restricted Persons are therefore prohibited from writing or buying such an option except under a Dealing Approval (or, for Other Restricted Persons, within a declared Trading Window). Note the put leg may separately offend the position-based short-selling ban in 2.2(b).
rules.evidence: Securities means shares, options, share rights ... and any other equity, debt or derivative instruments, or other linked financial instruments, including instruments to limit the economic risk of other securities held.

rules.detail: For personnel who are not Restricted Persons there is no clearance route, only the flat bans. A derivative that limits the exposure of unvested or holding-locked remuneration is a prohibited hedge, and any derivative position that would profit from a decline in the share price is prohibited short selling. Derivatives outside those two descriptions are not addressed for this tier.
rules.evidence: Greatland Personnel must not engage in: ... Short selling of Company Securities (that is, entering into a transaction or position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price of Company Securities).

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no approval route, on any arrangement having the effect of limiting exposure to risk relating to unvested remuneration. The Policy also notes that the Corporations Act independently prohibits such hedging by KMP (including Directors) and their closely related parties.
rules.evidence: Hedging transactions of Company Securities, meaning entering into an arrangement if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of the member to risk relating to an element of the person's remuneration that has not vested or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The hedging ban expressly extends to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a holding lock, so a collar over shares still inside a disposal restriction period is prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: an element of the person's remuneration that has not vested or has vested but remains subject to a holding lock

rules.detail: The express hedging ban is confined to unvested or holding-locked remuneration, so hedging fully vested and unrestricted shares is not itself prohibited. It remains a Dealing (an instrument to limit the economic risk of securities held is a Security) requiring a prior written Dealing Approval and, for non-PDMR Restricted Persons, a declared Trading Window. The put leg must still be tested against the short-selling ban in 2.2(b).
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons are also prohibited from Dealing in Company Securities unless permitted by the remainder of this Policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and equity swaps are not named. Each is caught as a Dealing: entering into a conditional agreement to sell Securities, and, under 8(a)(ii), any contractual arrangement by which the person may become contractually obliged to a third party to Deal. Prior Dealing Approval is required, and 8(c) says such approval should not be expected where the arrangement carries the risk of a forced trade in a Prohibited Period.
rules.evidence: otherwise transact, including (without limitation) using Securities as security for a loan or other obligation and entering into, amending or terminating any agreement (even if it is conditional) to subscribe for, buy or sell, or exercise or convert, any Securities

rules.detail: Flat prohibition applying to all Personnel including Restricted Persons, with no approval route. The definition is drafted by economic effect and by 'position', not by settlement or borrowing, so it is wide enough to capture a purchased put or any downside-profiting leg of a collar even where the shares are held outright.
rules.evidence: Short selling of Company Securities (that is, entering into a transaction or position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price of Company Securities).

rules.detail: Share loans are named only in the heading of Section 8; the operative text catches them as a contractual arrangement under which an entitlement to exercise a right attaching to the person's Company Securities is assigned to or exercisable by another party. Such Dealing is not permitted other than with a Dealing Approval, and 8(c) discourages approval.
rules.evidence: Dealing in Company Securities includes the grant of a security interest over Company Securities and any other contractual arrangement where: an entitlement to exercise a right attaching to Company Securities of a Restricted Person is assigned to or is exercisable by another party

rules.detail: CFDs are not named. A CFD is a derivative or linked financial instrument and so a Security, but a short CFD is a position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price of Company Securities and is therefore prohibited outright; a long CFD would be a Dealing requiring a Dealing Approval.
rules.evidence: entering into a transaction or position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price of Company Securities

rules.detail: Margin loans and margin calls are named in the Section 8 heading and margin call arrangements are expressly listed as arrangements under which the person may become contractually obliged to Deal. They are not banned outright, but are a Dealing requiring a Dealing Approval, and 8(c) warns that approval should not be expected because of the risk of a forced trade during a Prohibited Period.
rules.evidence: a Restricted Person may become contractually obliged to a third party to Deal in Company Securities, including but not limited to margin call arrangements.

rules.detail: Granting a security interest over Company Securities is expressly a Dealing, both under the general definition (using Securities as security for a loan or other obligation) and under Section 8(a). It is not permitted other than with a Dealing Approval; the same Dealing must be notified to the Company Secretary within two Business Days and, for Directors, announced to ASX.
rules.evidence: For the purposes of this Policy, Dealing in Company Securities includes the grant of a security interest over Company Securities

rules.detail: Using Securities as security for a loan or other obligation is a Dealing and is permitted only with a Dealing Approval. There is no outright ban, but 8(c) sets a strong presumption against approval for any arrangement carrying forced-trade risk, which is exactly the profile of a loan secured on collared shares with lender enforcement rights.
rules.evidence: A Dealing Approval under (b) should not be expected to be given to a Restricted Person having regard to the risk of a forced trade in Company Securities as part of the arrangement during a Prohibited Period, and the consequential legal and market reputational risk.

rules.detail: Section 8 is expressed to apply to Restricted Persons only; the Policy says nothing about secured financing by personnel who are not Restricted Persons, beyond the general requirement to Deal only in compliance with the Policy.

Short term buying and selling is prohibited for all Personnel, with selling within three months of buying given as guidance rather than a bright line. Restricted Persons seeking approval to sell must disclose when they last bought if relevant.
rules.evidence: Short term buying and selling of Company Securities. In considering what is “short term” for the purposes of this Policy, selling within three (3) months of buying securities in the Company is given as guidance.

clearance.approver: The Chair (or in their absence the Deputy Chair or Managing Director). The Chair must obtain approval from the Deputy Chair, or from the Managing Director and one non-executive Director jointly. No one may approve their own or an associate's Dealing.
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary; PDMRs and their PCAs also to the UK FCA on the PDMR notification form; Directors must complete an Appendix 3Y for ASX; the Company makes an RNS announcement
clearance.post_trade_deadline: Company Secretary within two Business Days of the Dealing (PCAs: immediately); FCA no later than three working days after the trade; RNS within two working days of receipt; ASX Appendix 3Y no more than five business days after the trade
clearance.evidence: Any Director, PDMR (as defined in Section 3.1(p) below) or Company Secretary, or any persons associated with them, must obtain Dealing Approval from the Chair (or in their absence by the Deputy Chair or Managing Director). ... A Dealing Approval is valid for two Business Days (excluding the day that the approval is received)

clearance.approver: The Managing Director for direct reports of the Managing Director; otherwise the Company Secretary (either may consult the Chair). No Dealing Approval is needed for Dealing during a Trading Window declared by the Chair.
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within two Business Days of the Dealing
clearance.evidence: During Trading Windows, Dealing in Company Securities by Restricted Persons (other than a Director, Company Secretary or other PDMR) is permitted, without a specific Dealing Approval.

clearance.approver: The Chair (or in their absence the Deputy Chair or Managing Director); during a MAR Closed Period or Prohibited Period approval will only be granted in exceptional circumstances
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary and the UK Financial Conduct Authority
clearance.post_trade_deadline: Company Secretary within two working days of the trade; FCA no later than three working days after the trade
clearance.evidence: During MAR Closed Periods, Dealing in Company Securities by PDMRs is prohibited other than pursuant to a Dealing Approval, which will only be granted in exceptional circumstances, such as those set out in Section 5(c) below.

In addition to the above prohibitions applicable to all Greatland Personnel, Restricted Persons are also prohibited from Dealing in Company Securities unless permitted by the remainder of this Policy.

short_term.basis: from purchase; expressed as guidance rather than a fixed rule
short_term.evidence: selling within three (3) months of buying securities in the Company is given as guidance

exceptions.approver: The person authorised to grant the Dealing Approval (Chair, Deputy Chair, Managing Director or Company Secretary as applicable)
exceptions.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order or other legal requirement to transfer Company securities.

exceptions.approver: The person authorised to grant the Dealing Approval
exceptions.evidence: compulsion by court order or other legal requirement to transfer Company securities

the mere take up of entitlements, or exercise of vested options, to subscribe for Company Securities under a pro rata rights issue to all shareholders, an employee share option plan (or similar) ... does not constitute a “Dealing”
the mere take up of Company Securities under a dividend re-investment plan (or similar) does not constitute a “Dealing” in Company Securities for the purpose of this Policy.

exceptions.approver: Chair (or Deputy Chair or Managing Director)
exceptions.evidence: where the beneficial interest in the relevant Company security does not change as a result of the transaction, but in each case only where the PDMR is able to demonstrate that the Dealing could not have been executed at another time

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No LVR, buffer or price-trigger guidance is given. Instead Section 8(c) states that a Dealing Approval for such an arrangement should not be expected, having regard to the risk of a forced trade during a Prohibited Period and the consequential legal and market reputational risk.
financing_disclosure: Restricted Persons; at inception (the grant of a security interest is itself a Dealing requiring prior Dealing Approval); Company Secretary (request cc'd to the Company Secretary, approval reported to the Board at its next meeting); before the arrangement is entered into
Restricted Persons; on completion of the Dealing; Company Secretary; within two Business Days of the Dealing
Directors; on completion of the Dealing; ASX via Appendix 3Y; no more than five business days after the trade

PDMRs and their persons closely associated; on completion of the Dealing; UK Financial Conduct Authority on the PDMR notification form, and RNS announcement by the Company; FCA within three working days, RNS within two working days of receipt

Employee share option plan / employee equity incentive scheme rules (referred to but not reproduced)
exemption_authority: The person authorised to grant a Dealing Approval (Chair, or in their absence Deputy Chair or Managing Director, for Directors/PDMRs/Company Secretary; Managing Director or Company Secretary for other Restricted Persons) may permit Dealing in a Closed Period, MAR Closed Period or Prohibited Period in exceptional circumstances, but only on sufficient evidence that the Dealing is the most reasonable course of action available, and approval must not be given where the approver has reason to believe the Dealing would breach the Policy, MAR or the other Regulations.
jurisdiction_overlays: UK Market Abuse Regulation: MAR Closed Periods (1 July / 31 December to publication of results), PDMR and PCA identification, notification and record-keeping
AIM Rules (Rule 21 dealing policy requirement; Rule 11 disclosure) as a company admitted to trading on the LSE AIM Market
UK Criminal Justice Act 1993 insider dealing offences
UK FCA notification of PDMR and PCA trades within three working days, and RNS announcement within two working days
Corporations Act 2001 (Cth), ASX Listing Rules and Appendix 3Y

bespoke_clauses.topic: short selling defined by economic position
bespoke_clauses.clause: Short selling of Company Securities (that is, entering into a transaction or position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price of Company Securities).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is drafted by economic effect and applies to every Greatland Personnel with no approval route, so the purchased put leg of a collar is arguably a prohibited 'position which would result in profiting from a decline', and the bank should get written confirmation that a covered protective put over shares actually held is not caught before proceeding.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities means ... any other equity, debt or derivative instruments, or other linked financial instruments, including instruments to limit the economic risk of other securities held.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both collar legs are Securities in their own right with no venue limitation, so entering, amending or terminating the OTC options is itself a Dealing requiring a fresh Dealing Approval at inception, on any roll or reset, and on unwind.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Dealing Approval under (b) should not be expected to be given to a Restricted Person having regard to the risk of a forced trade in Company Securities as part of the arrangement during a Prohibited Period, and the consequential legal and market reputational risk.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg is not banned outright but the Policy tells approvers to refuse it, so a funded collar depends on persuading the Chair that the bank's enforcement and physical-settlement rights are sufficiently constrained to avoid a forced trade in a Prohibited Period.

bespoke_clauses.topic: assignment of rights attaching to shares
bespoke_clauses.clause: any other contractual arrangement where: an entitlement to exercise a right attaching to Company Securities of a Restricted Person is assigned to or is exercisable by another party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Standard collar and security documentation that gives the bank voting, dividend or transfer rights over the collared shares is itself a Dealing needing approval, so the security package should leave those rights with the executive until enforcement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Closed Period means any time which is not a Trading Window or which is a MAR Closed Period. Trading Window means a period in which: in relation to a Director, Company Secretary or other PDMR, a Dealing Approval applies.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For Directors and PDMRs there is no standing open window at all: the only permitted execution period is the two Business Days of a specific Dealing Approval, which can be shortened in writing at any time, so pricing and signing of every collar step must be compressed into that window.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Dealing Approval request by a PDMR during a MAR Closed Period or a Prohibited Period will only be granted in exceptional circumstances such as: severe financial hardship which requires the immediate Dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Between 1 July and the annual results and between 31 December and the half-year results, no collar step by a PDMR can be executed unless it meets the MAR exceptional-circumstances test, which a voluntary financing structure will not.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (The Corporations Act also prohibits such hedging transactions for persons who have authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the entity (including Directors) and their closely related parties.)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For KMP and their closely related parties the ban on hedging unvested or holding-locked remuneration is statutory as well as contractual, so no company approval could cure a collar over that portion of the holding.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Greatland Personnel must not ... place themselves in a position where it may reasonably be perceived that they have Dealt in Company Securities, other than in compliance with this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Reputational perception is an independent breach standard, and Section 5(a)(iii) makes 'adverse reputational imputations' a stated ground for refusing approval, which is a live risk for a publicly disclosable director collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons means ... and persons associated with them (including close family; entities, trusts or investment vehicles over which they exercise control or material influence or of which they are a beneficiary; and business or other associates).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust, SPV or investment vehicle does not avoid the Dealing Approval requirement or the disclosure obligations.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The issue of a Dealing Approval is to be reported to the Board at the next Board meeting. The Company Secretary will maintain a written record of Dealing Approval requests and responses.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any approved collar becomes a matter of Board record as well as market disclosure, so the transaction cannot be kept confidential within the company.

summary: A funded collar over fully vested, unrestricted shares is theoretically available to a Restricted Person but only on tight conditions and with real legal risk. Every element - the OTC put and call (Securities in their own right, expressly including 'instruments to limit the economic risk of other securities held'), the grant of a security interest, and any arrangement that could oblige the executive to Deal - is a Dealing requiring prior written Dealing Approval from the Chair (Managing Director or Company Secretary for other Restricted Persons), valid only two Business Days and revocable, with notification to the Company Secretary within two Business Days and ASX Appendix 3Y, FCA and RNS disclosure for Directors and PDMRs. Two provisions are close to fatal: Section 8(c) says a Dealing Approval for a secured or forced-trade-risk arrangement 'should not be expected to be given', and Section 2.2(b) bans, for all Personnel with no approval route, any 'transaction or position which would result in profiting from a decline in the price' of the shares, which on its face reaches the purchased put. Any shares that are unvested or vested but subject to a holding lock cannot be collared at all, that ban being both contractual and statutory for KMP. As a dual ASX/AIM issuer the company also imposes MAR Closed Periods from 1 July and 31 December until the respective results, during which a PDMR can only deal in exceptional circumstances, and for Directors and PDMRs there is no standing open window at all.
